bounded_statement: The selected result in results/report.md comes from an independent-two-sample t-test in which each of the 12 distinct `k1`,`k2` source items contributes one entry to `left` (column `a`) and one entry to `right` (column `b`); the same authorized independent unit therefore enters the row-independent procedure twice, and the reported df=22.0 asserts 24 independent observations drawn from only 12 units.

counterevidence_considered.description: Every ordered `k1`,`k2` pair occurs exactly once, so no unit is duplicated across rows; the repeated entry arises across the two measurement columns of a single row, not from row-level replication.

The `tag` column is unique per row (t01..t12) and thus offers no competing clustering structure that could be blamed for the dependence; the dependence is entirely the within-row pairing of `a` and `b`.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: tag values t01..t12, one per row

evidence.description: task.md fixes the authorized independent unit as the ordered `k1`,`k2` pair, so the two numeric fields on a row are measurements of the same unit.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. Treat each distinct ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as one source item; rows carrying the same ordered pair originate from the same source item.

evidence.description: Both arms are built by iterating the same staged row sequence, one arm per column, so each row (unit) supplies exactly one entry to each arm.
evidence.observed_value: left from column a, right from column b, same `staged` list

source_refs.quoted_text:
staged = rows
left = [float(row["a"]) for row in staged]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in staged]

evidence.description: The named procedure is the independent-samples t-test, which treats every entry in the two arms as an independent observation.
The staged file supplies 12 rows / 12 source items and therefore 24 measurements in total.
The reported degrees of freedom make the double entry explicit and quantify the resulting inflation of the effective sample size.
evidence.observed_value: df=22.0 = 24 - 2, versus 11 df for 12 independent units analysed within-unit

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: To falsify, I searched the staged file for any repeated ordered `k1`,`k2` pair, since the most literal form of this class is one unit appearing in several rows; none exists, and the workflow performs no filtering, deduplication or aggregation (`staged = rows`), so under a strictly row-duplication reading the finding would not stand. I then tried to explain away the surviving mechanism: if `a` and `b` originated from different source items, the two arms would be independent, but task.md states the ordered pair identifies the source item and each row carries a single pair together with both `a` and `b`, so the arms are matched measurements on the same 12 units. I also checked whether the report could still be a unit-respecting analysis despite the code: df=22.0 equals n1+n2-2 for 12+12 entries and could only arise from treating all 24 measurements as independent, and `ttest_ind` provides no within-unit correction. No alternative reading of the visible files reconciles 24 independent observations with 12 authorized units, so the verdict survives every falsification route available in these files.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py forms both comparison arms from two columns of the identical staged row list and passes them to `scipy.stats.ttest_ind`, whose independence assumption requires every entry in both arms to come from a distinct unit. Since task.md designates each ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as one source item, `a` and `b` on a row are repeated measurements of one unit; the workflow neither pairs them nor reduces each unit to a single entry.
